Subject: Renewal options and smoothing for your mid-year capacity increase

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I put together two practical paths to handle the mid-contract uplift you mentioned while keeping the renewal co-term simple on Jan 1. High level: one option keeps an annualized top-up (fast capacity + smaller uplift discount), the other uses a hybrid credit bridge that staggers consumption buckets to reduce up-front cost.

Attached: renewal_scenarios_v2.xlsx (three worked examples) and a draft SOW. Quick summary below:

1) Annualized top-up (Option A)
- Immediate +25% capacity add-on billed pro-rata for the remainder of the term
- Apply a 10% uplift discount on the incremental capacity for the remainder of the year
- Co-term on Jan 1 with full annualized commit at renewal price

2) Hybrid credit bridge (Option B) — recommended if you prefer smoothing spend
- Split the requested uplift into two buckets: 60% capacity committed now, 40% as a voucher (12-month expiry) you draw down as usage grows
- Voucher priced at a blended discount (15% off list) and recognized at drawdown; initial commit gets a 7% uplift discount
- This reduces near-term cash while preserving access to capacity spikes

Action items: can you confirm whether finance prefers an immediate invoice or a voucher approach? If you want, we can prepare a one-page amendment that toggles between options based on your selection.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

— Tessa

Alyssa — great questions. Answers below and I added a sample invoice cadence to the attached workbook (see tab: cashflow_examples).

- Voucher minimums: no hard minimum draw. Voucher is valid for 12 months. If at 12 months you have unused voucher value we offer a 50% credit-back of remaining voucher value applied to next term (this was negotiated for similar accounts to reduce waste).
- Overages above voucher: usage beyond the voucher/bucket is billed at standard per-token rates; if you draw beyond committed capacity consistently we recommend converting to committed capacity at forthcoming renewal for a blended rate.
- Reassignment: vouchers are assignable across Nimbus legal entities under the same contract; we will include a short clause in the amendment.

Given your preference to avoid up-front cash, Option B keeps near-term invoice lower. I've also flagged the hybrid proposal for a one-time approval with finance to accept the 50% unused-voucher protection.

If helpful, Ben — I’ve sketched the pricing math. Can you confirm we can offer the 15% voucher discount + 7% initial-commit uplift within our guide?

— Tessa

Tessa / Lauren / Vivek — quick internal note: I reviewed the numbers. We can approve:
- Voucher discount at 15% (max) with the 50% unused-credit protection carve-out
- Initial commit uplift discount at 7% for the 60% committed bucket
- Voucher must have 12-mo expiry and be transferable within the legal entity group only

Two items to flag for legal/finance: include clear definitions for "unused voucher" (monetary value vs tokens) and a cap on future reassignments (single reassignment allowed). Also, we should lock in a one-time amendment that auto-expands price if they convert voucher to committed capacity mid-term (to avoid retroactive deep discounts).

If no objections I can sign off and we can send the updated SOW + DocuSign link to Nimbus.
